name: skate-park
description: A painterly third-person skateboarding game for the browser: a beachside park at golden hour, built with three.js, TypeScript and Vite.

paragraphs: A third-person skateboarding game for the browser, built in three.js. A small flow park sits behind a beach boardwalk at golden hour, painted in a soft, warm, hand-made look, and you skate it as Sol, an original character: push and carve, pump the transitions, drop in from the deck, ollie and flip, grind the rails and ledges, manual, bail and get back up, then turn the sky to sunset, blue hour or noon. There are no levels, timers or goals; trick names and a combo score pop up and fade, and that is all the game keeps. The park, the beach town around it and the board are built in code, Sol's…

It plays on a computer with a keyboard (the mouse and a gamepad are optional) and on phones and tablets with touch controls. It was built in Chrome on Windows, on a PC with an RTX 4060 and a 200 Hz monitor; the phone version was tested in Chrome's device emulation with a slowed-down CPU, not yet on a real phone. The first visit downloads about 1.9 MB before the game starts: on the live site, in Chrome's Fast 4G emulation with a four times slower CPU, it was playable after 4.6 s with the Android profile and 6.1 s with the iPhone profile. The crowd and the sounds stream in after that. On load…

The edges are seat steps, planters and benches, and three murals cover the outer wall of the half pipe, a small pavilion and the snack kiosk.
